facts_of_case: Two women, Indu and Reeta, were married to Bharat at different times. Ex-parte decree of divorce was passed by the Court. The marriage of Bharat with Reeta is alleged to be in contravention of section 15 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A party aggrieved by an ex-parte decree has two concurrent remedies in law.
legal_principles.held: A party aggrieved by such decree may also make an application for setting aside the ex-parte decree to the Court which passed the decree or to the transferee Court in case the jurisdiction of the Court which passed the decree originally is transferred to some other Court.

legal_principles.principle: The fact that the party to the original marriage has re-married is not decisive for determination of the proceedings adopted by the spouse against whom ex-parte decree of divorce was passed.
legal_principles.held: The fact that the party to the original marriage has re-married is not decisive for determination of the proceedings adopted by the spouse against whom ex-parte decree of divorce was passed.

outcome.final_order: The ex-parte decree for divorce was set aside. The marriage of Bharat with Reeta is alleged to be in contravention of section 15 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
